body.p: Applicant submits this Reply in response to the Office Action mailed March 10, 2022.
I. Status of the Claims

By this Reply, Applicant cancels amends claims 1, 4, 7, 9, 12, 15, 17, and 20. The originally filed specification and drawings fully support the subject matter of the amended and new claims. Claims 1-20 are pending in this application. Claims 1, 9, and 17 are the sole independent claims. II. Section 112(a) Rejections

In the Office Action, claims 1-20 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(a) for allegedly failing to comply with the written description requirement. (Office Action at pages 2-3.) In particular, the Office Action refers to passages of the claims reciting "determining a threshold blood flow characteristic based on the patient-specific anatomic model of the patient's bowel and a predetermined healthy or average blood flow characteristic based on a population-based measurement or estimate," as allegedly being unsupported by the specification. In particular, the Office Action asserts:
... the published Specification, para. 0046 and 0048, fails to
provide such written description support because the
specification teaches an average blood flow characteristic
and teaches a predetermined threshold blood flow
characteristic. The average blood flow characteristic is determined from a population-based measurement or
estimate. However, the predetermined threshold blood flow
characteristic is defined as where a patient blood flow rate below a given value of q may signify an inadequate blood
supply to a respective tissue region of the patient.
Accordingly, the Specification fails to provide the necessary
written description for a threshold blood flow characteristic
based on (a) the patient-specific anatomic model of the
patient's bowel and (b) a predetermined healthy or average
blood flow characteristic based on a population-based
measurement or estimate
Applicant respectfully traverses this rejection and submits that the claims are fully supported by the specification.

The purpose of the adequate written description requirement is to ensure that the inventor had possession of the claimed subject matter at the time the application was filed. See M.P.E.P. § 2163. If a person of ordinary skill in the art would have understood the inventor to have been in possession of the claimed invention at the time of the filing, even if every nuance of the claims is not explicitly described in the specification, then the adequate written description requirement is met. In re Alton, 76 F.3d 1168, 1175, 37 U.S.P.Q.2d 1578, 1581 (Fed. Cir. 1996). The written description requirement may be satisfied using words, structures, figures, diagrams, and formulas. See M.P.E.P. § 2163(1) (citing Lockwood v. American Airlines, Inc., 107 F.3d 1565, 1572, 41 USPQ2d 1961, 1966 (Fed. Cir. 1997)). Indeed, in some circumstances, "drawings alone may provide a 'written description' of an invention as required by §112." Vas-Cath, Inc. v. Mahurkar, 935 F.2d 1555, 1565, 19 USPQ2d 1111, 1118 (Fed. Cir. 1991).
Additionally, "[t]he examiner has the initial burden of presenting by a

preponderance of evidence why a person skilled in the art would not recognize in an applicant's disclosure a description of the invention defined by the claims." See M.P.E.P. § 2163(III)(A). In rejecting claims under Section 112, first paragraph, the examiner "must set forth express findings of fact regarding the [] analysis which supports the lack of written description conclusions." Id. In addition to identifying the claim limitation at issue, these findings should "[e]stablish a prima facie case by

providing reasons why a person skilled in the art at the time the application was filed would not have recognized that the inventor was in possession of the invention as claimed in view of the disclosure of the application as filed." Id.

To that end, the disclosure of, for example, paragraph [0046] in the present application provides adequate support for the phrase "determining a threshold blood flow characteristic based on the patient-specific anatomic model of the patient's bowel and a predetermined healthy or average blood flow characteristic based on a population-based measurement or estimate," as recited by the independent claims. Paragraph [0046] in the present application states:
Step 305 may include determining an average blood flow
characteristic or predetermined threshold blood flow
characteristic of one or more locations in the modeled vasculature. For example, a location in the modeled
vasculature may have a healthy or average blood flow
rate q, determined from a population-based
measurement or estimate. Alternatively or in addition, q
may be a predetermined threshold blood flow rate, where a patient blood flow rate below a given value of q may signify an inadequate blood supply to a respective tissue region of
the patient. In one embodiment, the average blood flow
characteristic or predetermined threshold blood flow
characteristic may be associated with the one or more
locations of interest within the bowel region (e.g., from step

(Emphasis added.) Here, the specification states that, for "a location in the modeled vasculature," the value "q" may be both "a healthy or average blood flow rate q, determined from a population-based measurement or estimate" and "a predetermined threshold blood flow rate" where "q" may be "associated with the one or more locations of interest within the bowel region." In view of this, Applicant requests that this rejection be withdrawn.

The dependent claims were not specifically addressed in the 35 U.S.C. § 112(a) rejection mentioned above, and were apparently rejected solely due to their dependence from the rejected independent claims. As discussed above, the independent claims are fully supported and in compliance with 35 U.S.C. § 112(a). Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of the § 112(a) rejection. III. Section 103 Rejections
In the Office Action, claims 1-7, 9-15, and 17-20 were rejected under 35 U.S.C.

§ 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Taylor (US 2012/0041318) in view of Walker (Walker, T Gregory. "Mesenteric vasculature and collateral pathways" Seminars in interventional radiology vol. 26, 3 (2009): 167-74) and John (US 2007/0208263). (Office Action at pages 4-16.) Claims 8 and 16 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Taylor in view of Walker and John, and further in view of Cleveland Clinic (Cleveland Clinic "Intestinal Ischemic Syndrome", https://my.clevelandclinic.org/services/heart/disorders/arterial-disease/intestinal- ischemic-syndrome). (Office Action at pages 16-17.) The rejections are respectfully traversed.
In rejecting claim 1, the Office Action acknowledged that Taylor in view of Walker does not expressly disclose:
determining a threshold blood flow characteristic based on the patient-specific anatomic model of the patient's bowel
and a predetermined healthy or average blood flow
characteristic based on a population-based measurement or
estimate
as previously recited by claim 1. (Office Action at page 11.) Instead, the Office Action asserted that paragraphs [0071]-[0075] of John compensate for these deficiencies

because it discloses: "The reference data of the reference value module 552 can be threshold values, which can be based upon self- or population-norm data." (Office Action at page 12.) Applicant does not agree with the characterizations of the claims and cited references set forth in the Office Action. However, in the interest of advancing prosecution, claim 1 is amended herein to recite:

SVG {EMBED HERE} 0.8872.687
aracteristic based on

tomic model of the
healthy or average
population-based
The cited references fail to disclose these features of amended claim 1.
For example, The cited portion of John discloses: "The reference data of the

reference value module 552 can be threshold values, which can be based upon self- or population-norm data," and further describes that "the normative data can include data obtained during one or more interventions such as during angioplasty." (John, paragraph [0071].) Even if the "reference data of the reference value module" is construed to be a "threshold blood flow characteristic," as recited by amended claim 1, which Applicant does not admit, John expressly discloses that the "reference data of the reference value module" is obtained entirely by invasive means such as angioplasty. John fails to disclose that such data is based on a "non-invasive patient-specific anatomic model," as recited by amended claim 1.

Accordingly, John does not compensate for the deficiencies of Taylor in view of Walker with respect to these features of claim 1. The remaining cited references fail to compensate for the noted deficiencies of Taylor in view of Walker and John, and
therefore, claim 1 is patentably distinguishable over the cited references for at least these reasons.

The above comments are specifically directed to independent claim 1. However, it is respectfully submitted that the comments would be helpful in understanding various differences of the other independent claims over the cited references. Therefore, it is

respectfully submitted that all the independent claims are patentable over the cited references. Moreover, it is respectfully submitted that the various dependent claims arepatentable over the cited references for at least the reason that they depend from anindependent claim that is patentable over the cited references.
In view of the above, it is respectfully submitted that the rejection is overcome. IV. After Final Consideration Pilot

Applicant requests that this application be considered under the After Final Consideration Pilot Program 2.0 at the USPTO. A Certification and Request for Consideration Under the After Final Consideration Pilot Program 2.0 is being filed herewith. Applicant appreciates the Examiner's consideration of this Reply under that Program.
V. Conclusion

The Office Action contains characterizations of the claims and the related art with which the applicant does not necessarily agree. Unless expressly noted otherwise, applicant declines to subscribe to any statement or characterization in the Office Action.
In discussing the specification, claims, and drawings in this Reply, it is to be
understood that Applicant is in no way intending to limit the scope of the claims to any exemplary embodiments described in the specification or abstract and/or shown in the
drawings. Rather, Applicant is entitled to have the claims interpreted broadly to the maximum extent permitted by statute, regulation, and applicable case law.
Applicant respectfully requests that this Reply under 37 C.F.R. § 1.116 be

entered by the Examiner, placing the claims in condition for allowance. The proposed claim amendments do not raise new issues or necessitate the undertaking of any additional search of the art by the Examiner. Therefore, this Reply should allow for immediate action by the Examiner.
Furthermore, Applicant respectfully points out that the final Office Action

presented new arguments as to the application of the art against the pending claims. It is respectfully submitted that the entering of this Reply would allow Applicant to respond to the final rejection and place the application in condition for allowance.
Finally, Applicant submits that the entry of this Reply would place the application in better form for appeal, should the Examiner dispute the patentability of the pending claims.

In view of the foregoing remarks, Applicant submits that this claimed invention is neither anticipated nor rendered obvious in view of the prior art references cited against this application. Applicant therefore requests the reconsideration and reexamination of the application, and the timely allowance of the pending claims.
